replies.description: how the session writes replies: terse bans the words a, an, the, is, are, was and were; tight drops preamble, recap and filler; standard keeps full prose

rules.terse: Replies are terse: chat prose only, in the user's language. In chat prose, lists and numbered steps included, never write a, an or the, and never write is, are, was or were; fragments, `→` for leads to and `=` for is are fine. Example: "The hook is not reading the setting, so the reminder never fires." becomes "Hook not reading setting → reminder never fires." Code, commands, paths, identifiers, error text, numbers and every not, no, only and except stay whole. Full sentences return only for a security warning, a confirmation before an irreversible action and a question to the user; a label such as `Warning:` on anything else does not lift the ban. Commits, PR text, docs, code comments and saved files keep normal prose. A lone `?` from the user asks for the previous reply in full. The output style sets the layout; this sets how dense the words are.
rules.tight: Replies are tight: no preamble, recap, filler or hedging. Code, commands, paths, identifiers, error text, numbers, warnings and every not, no, only and except stay whole, and a security warning or a confirmation before an irreversible action is written in full sentences. The output style sets the layout; this sets how dense the words are.
rules.standard: Replies are standard: full prose. The output style sets the layout; this sets how dense the words are.

budget.description: high: medium, except the deep branch review, the design critique and the hardest work dispatch their xhigh twins. medium: every agent dispatch uses the model its kind resolves to in lib/model-kinds.json. low: an agent whose kind resolves to a tier named under budgets in lib/model-kinds.json dispatches on that tier's replacement instead, except the hardest work, which dispatches its medium-effort twin. The old names full, normal and lean still read as high, medium and low

rules.high: Budget is high: when you dispatch exo:review-branch-deep, exo:critique-ui or exo:solve-hard, dispatch exo:review-branch-deep-high, exo:critique-ui-high or exo:solve-hard-high in its place, with the same prompt; no model is replaced.
rules.low: Budget is low: when you dispatch exo:solve-hard, dispatch exo:solve-hard-low in its place, with the same prompt, and leave its model as the agent sets it. When the Task tool dispatches any other plugin agent whose kind in lib/model-kinds.json resolves to model {from} (the kind is the agent's entry under agents, looked up under kinds, whose tier the provider named at the top maps to a model under providers), pass {to} as the Task call's own model parameter instead.
